hints.title: Max Frequency Chunk Arrangement Strategy
hints.text: The most frequent tasks dictate the minimum execution frame structure due to the cooldown constraint n. How can arranging the highest frequency tasks frame the timeline?

hints.title: Idle Gap Filling Capacity Invariant
hints.text: The bottleneck is the maximum frequency task count, which creates chunks separated by n intervals; lower frequency tasks fill the idle gaps.

hints.title: Chunk Idle Slot Calculation Procedure
hints.text: Count frequencies of each task. Find the maximum frequency and how many distinct tasks achieve that maximum frequency. Calculate minimum required slots based on chunks and idle filling. Return the maximum of this formula and total task count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def leastInterval(self, tasks: List[str], n: int) -> int:
        counts = {}
        for t in tasks:
            counts[t] = counts.get(t, 0) + 1
        max_freq = max(counts.values())
        max_count = sum(1 for v in counts.values() if v == max_freq)
        part_count = max_freq - 1
        empty_slots = part_count * (n - (max_count - 1))
        available_tasks = len(tasks) - max_freq * max_count
        idles = max(0, empty_slots - available_tasks)
        return len(tasks) + idles
```

variables: N: input array length or bit count
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating every minute step-by-step with state tracking can be slow for large cooling periods n.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting 26 character frequencies operates in O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should formulate the math equation (max_freq - 1) * (n + 1) + max_count and take the max with total tasks.
